text: The access entries of this legacy key reach rwb-decision as DecisionRecorded messages on the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1, written by the serving service in its own schema, and rwb-decision keeps the central ledger copy in rwb_decision.decision_log_entry; the grant, its time box, the permission matrix and the masking policy stay with rwb-access and are never read from a table here.
why: The legacy story wrote every access event in process into one decision_log_entry in the single recovery schema; under DP-01, DP-03 and ADR-022 no service may write another's table, so the only shape left is the local record of the serving service plus the shared topic, with the central ledger as the consumer.
read: Architecture v5 slides 13, 28 and 42; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 rows DP-01 and DP-03 and R3 default rulings; context pack P7 (shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1, one login per service); legacy RWB-E1-039 sections 1, 3 and 12.
confirm: Architecture owner confirms the ingest route of the access entries at the wave 1 design review
impact: If the ingest were a call into rwb-decision, the serving service would need a write operation that the Ownership Map does not carry, and the fail-closed rule of the serving service would depend on another service's transaction.

text: The actions element of an access entry carries at least the legacy-named facts (area, right, result, field IDs with their masking flag, filter, row count, document ID, reason code, grant ID, incident reference), and the decision-log read answers the grant, the incident and the review due time of an entry under the read elements grantId, incidentReference and reviewDueAt as working names until the contract baseline publishes them.
why: The legacy story names the content of actions in words and the TSD declares the decision-log read without those three elements; the review of a break-glass use needs all three on one answer, so they are named here rather than left out.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-039 sections 11 and 12; TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 (API-P7-006, API-P7-007); Template and Rules v1 R9; context pack P7 (ownership rows of P7).
confirm: Contract baseline of RWB-P7-E2005-CON or the API specification owner fixes the three element names
impact: A different published name changes the read's answer and the assertions of AC4 and AC6 only; no stored column and no migration is affected.

text: The review due time of a break-glass activation is computed on the read from the entry's decided_at plus the parameter rwb.access.breakglass.review-days (legacy assumed value 1), and is never stored as a column of decision_log_entry.
why: The legacy story sets a review window as a parameter (DL38) and BR7 requires each use to be reviewed inside it; a stored due time would freeze the parameter value of the day and would need a migration when the window changes.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-039 sections 3, 8 (BR5, BR7) and 13; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 row DP-06; context pack P7 (parameters contract of rwb-case).
confirm: Business owner of the access module confirms the review window is read at query time
impact: A stored due time would add one column and one migration to this story and would fix the window per entry at write time.

text: A record whose access element is missing or invalid is refused with the legacy identifier MSG-P7-009 and the field name, while MSG-P7-003 stays the message of an action that could not be recorded and MSG-P4-002 the refusal of a caller without the Decision log right; the published catalogue entry format of the three identifiers is not fixed by any source read here.
why: The legacy story carries the three identifiers with their texts and no catalogue; the ledger needs one refusal identifier for a malformed access record and one for a failed append, and reusing the legacy pair keeps the vocabulary of RWB-P4-E1039-APP unchanged.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-039 section 14; FSD P7 v3 A2.1.3.1 and A2.2.3.1 (VR-P7-001-2, VR-P7-002-2); Template and Rules v1 R9.
confirm: Message catalogue owner publishes the entry format and the identifiers for the service
impact: A catalogue that assigns a different identifier changes the text of section 14 and the assertions of AC5, AC6 and AC8; no behaviour changes.
